name: anomaly-route-loop
description: Route loop detection test. Bramble's RREP routing prevents loops under normal conditions; this scenario uses kill/rejoin churn of the central relay C to attempt creating stale cross-routes while real traffic flows before, between, and after the cycles. Loops in practice require packet corruption, race conditions, or implementation bugs, so zero route_loop anomalies over a run that really delivers is the expected result and validates the routing design; the detector (checked at each relay's forward, keyed on arriving hop_limit) is the safety net this scenario keeps honest. Radio runs SF7/250kHz so frame airtime is far below the RREQ forward-jitter window: B and D are mutually hidden same-hop relays, and at slower rates their jittered rebroadcasts always overlap at the funnel C, jamming every discovery (the #173 failure mode) before any loop question can even be asked.
